title: Orbes unveils Exo-ORB and agreement with Symphony Space
summary: Orbes, a Southern California startup, unveiled Exo-ORB, a free-flying satellite, and announced an agreement to send it to gather imagery of an uncrewed Symphony Space station. The partnership aims to support Symphony Space's operations.

title: Intel debuts new chip for space computing
summary: Intel has introduced a new chip named Starfire designed for space computing, enabling onboard data processing and AI workloads. This development marks a significant advancement in the space industry's technological capabilities.

title: SpaceNews Welcomes Max Aliprandi as Business Development Associate
summary: SpaceNews announced the hiring of Max Aliprandi as Business Development Associate to strengthen their sales and business development teams. This move supports the company's expansion efforts and audience growth.

title: Amazon files application for direct-to-device satellite constellation
summary: Amazon has filed an application with the FCC for a constellation of over 5,100 satellites to provide direct-to-device services using Globalstar spectrum. This move aims to expand Amazon's satellite connectivity capabilities.

title: Blue Origin to test New Glenn upper stages at Stennis
summary: Blue Origin will utilize NASA's Stennis Space Center for testing New Glenn upper stages while simultaneously reconstructing its Cape Canaveral launch site. This move supports the development of the company's heavy-lift rocket.

title: Rocket Lab to open Alaska launch site under $266 million Space Force deal
summary: Rocket Lab will establish a new launch site in Alaska under a $266 million contract with the U.S. Space Force. The facility in Kodiak will support up to 18 suborbital missions for military testing.

title: AI in orbit is a double-edged sword. Here’s how to keep it from cutting space cooperation apart
summary: The article discusses the dual-use nature of AI in space, highlighting its potential to disrupt international cooperation if misused. It suggests that treaties or voluntary agreements are necessary to prevent an arms race in space.

title: NASA and ESA facilities avoid major damage from wildfires in Spain
summary: NASA and ESA ground stations in Spain avoided serious damage from wildfires. The facilities are critical for space operations.

title: SpaceX conducts 13th Starship test flight
summary: SpaceX successfully conducted the 13th suborbital test flight of its Starship on July 24, addressing issues from the previous flight and deploying functioning satellites for the first time.

title: ULA deals with financial challenges caused by Vulcan grounding
summary: United Launch Alliance secured a loan from its corporate parents to address financial challenges stemming from the grounding of its Vulcan Centaur rocket. The company is navigating the impact of the rocket's delay on its operations.

title: Curiosity Mars rover inspects cracked wheel | Space photo of the day for July 24, 2026
summary: NASA's Curiosity Mars rover shows significant wear on its wheels after nearly 14 years on Mars. New images highlight the damage sustained during its mission.

title: X-ray spacecraft finds supermassive black hole stirring up the 'red potato' galaxy: 'There may be a cook in this cosmic kitchen'
summary: Astronomers using the Chandra X-ray spacecraft discovered a jet from a supermassive black hole stirring gas in a galaxy nicknamed the 'red potato'. The findings suggest dynamic activity in the galaxy's core.

title: Private companies could ruin the night sky for the entire world, and international law can't stop them
summary: Private companies may significantly alter the night sky globally, and the U.S. FCC has unilateral authority to approve space projects. International law lacks the power to prevent these changes.

title: A seed that flew around the moon grew into this tree in NYC
summary: A tree grown from a seed that orbited the moon was unveiled in NYC's Madison Square Park. The event took place during a smoky birthday party.

title: I'm not an astronaut, but I went to the International Space Station (sort of)
summary: A non-astronaut experienced a simulated visit to the International Space Station, highlighting its continued existence as a marvel. The statement emphasizes the station's ongoing significance.

title: We talk with astronaut Michael Foale about the 1997 Space Station Mir crisis: 'He took all the blame of the collision on his shoulders'
summary: Astronaut Michael Foale reflects on the 1997 Space Station Mir crisis, taking full responsibility for a collision and crediting the crew with saving the station. He emphasizes the teamwork that prevented disaster during the incident.

title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 220 — First on Mars
summary: The 220th episode of the 'This Week In Space' podcast commemorates the 50th anniversary of Viking 1's Mars landing, featuring discussions with Dr. Pascal Lee and Dr. Penny Boston.

title: An off-the-shelf camera could help us find more black holes smashing together
summary: A new off-the-shelf camera could enhance the detection of black hole collisions without requiring new technology development. This innovation addresses an instrumentation challenge for LIGO.

title: NASA’s Hubble Shows Star Formation in Andromeda Galaxy Winding Down
summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has observed a significant 500-million-year decline in star formation activity within the Andromeda galaxy. This finding provides new insights into the galaxy's evolutionary processes.

title: NASA Astronaut Chris Williams, Crewmates Return from Space Station
summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Roscosmos cosmonauts concluded an eight-month science mission aboard the International Space Station and returned to Earth safely. The crew landed in Kazakhstan after departing the space station.

title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Snaps Family Portrait of Earth, Moon
summary: NASA's ESCAPADE spacecraft captured images of Earth and the Moon during its journey to Mars. The photos were taken from a distance of 363,250 miles from Earth and 115,600 miles from the Moon.

title: New Crew Members Welcomed to International Space Station
summary: Three new crew members—Anna Kikina and Pyotr Dubrov of Roscosmos and Anil Menon of NASA—arrived at the International Space Station on July 14, 2026. They were welcomed aboard the station on July 18, 2026.

title: NASA Announces New Spacecraft Technology Demonstration Mission at Moon
summary: NASA has awarded a contract to Advanced Space for the CAPSTONE 02 mission to demonstrate advanced spacecraft technologies near the Moon. The mission aims to test rendezvous operations, autonomous navigation, and cislunar communication as part of Artemis program infrastructure.

title: NASA to Support Blue Origin New Glenn Rocket Testing, Advance Artemis
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have agreed to conduct second stage hot fire testing for the New Glenn rocket at NASA's Stennis Space Center. This collaboration supports NASA's Artemis program and reinforces their partnership.

title: Hubble Spies One-Sided Spiral
summary: The Hubble Space Telescope captured an image of spiral galaxy NGC 4654, which is located 72 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. The galaxy's asymmetric structure is highlighted in the observation.

title: A Million-Panel Project
summary: Utah inaugurated a large-scale solar power and battery storage facility, featuring a million-panel array. The project is one of the biggest in the region.

title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4954–4960: Celebrating Our Rover Engineers Past and Present
summary: The Curiosity rover team celebrates the contributions of past and present engineers. The blog highlights the APXS instrument's role in measuring rock chemistry during recent operations.

title: Look for NASA+ Now Streaming on Amazon Fire TV
summary: NASA's streaming service, NASA+, is now available on Amazon Fire TV Channels, expanding access to its content via Alexa+. Future programming may include science mission launches and test flights.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft has revealed surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io after two flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the moon's volcanic activity and geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket on the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn rocket for its upcoming missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX on its third attempt. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's development of the Starship program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully docked at the International Space Station (ISS), expanding the station's crew. A U.S. spacewalk also completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay is due to the need for further validation before the next attempt.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch Northrop Grumman's MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft from Florida. This mission marks a significant step in on-orbit servicing technology.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9, Starship, and Chinese rockets scheduled to launch
summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new attempt at launching Starship Flight 13 after a previous aborted launch. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are also scheduled for upcoming launches.

title: Making Progress: Relativity’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and PLD Space’s Miura 5
summary: Three companies—Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space—are making progress with their new rocket developments: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5, respectively. This comes amid increased attention on SpaceX's Starship test program.

title: China’s first recovered booster returns to port as LandSpace aims for first land recovery
summary: China achieved a significant milestone with the first successful recovery of its booster, which has now returned to port. LandSpace is now aiming for the first land recovery of a booster.

title: Soyuz MS-29 launches new crew to ISS from Baikonur
summary: Soyuz MS-29 successfully launched a new crew to the International Space Station (ISS) from Baikonur Cosmodrome on July 14. This marks another mission to sustain operations and research aboard the orbital laboratory.

summary: The TEC Business to Business website reported on a space industry news article, but no specific details were provided.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication underscores the agency's significant contributions to space exploration and technology over five decades.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with the European space industry on September 16–17. The event aims to exchange ideas, highlight capabilities, and explore new opportunities.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technology for next-generation antennas, highlighting innovations in the space industry. It emphasizes the role of silicon in improving antenna performance and efficiency.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: The European Space Agency's PLATO spacecraft has completed electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber at ESTEC, confirming its electronics are space-ready. The mission is now cleared for launch on an Ariane 6 rocket by Arianespace in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies.

title: The art of hadrons
summary: The news headline 'The art of hadrons' suggests a creative or artistic interpretation of particle physics, likely related to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) or hadron collider research. The accompanying image hints at a visual representation of hadrons.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting events to discuss the implementation of CM25, the Council Meeting at Ministerial Level 2025, focusing on industrial opportunities and thematic priorities. These events aim to engage industry in ESA programs and facilitate direct dialogue.

title: One robotic arm to rule them all
summary: The article discusses a new robotic arm designed for versatile applications in the space industry. It highlights the potential of this technology to revolutionize various space operations.

title: We’re back: Proba-3 ready for more science
summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and its ASPIICS instrument are fully operational, resuming formation flying to create artificial eclipses for scientific observations.

title: ORBES Unveils Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft
summary: ORBES introduced the Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft, a 12U, sub-26-kg spacecraft designed for on-board customer infrastructure inspection. The spacecraft is intended to launch and provide ready-to-go inspection capabilities.

title: Starship Sticks the Water Landing on Flight 13
summary: SpaceX successfully completed the 13th test flight of its Starship rocket, achieving its first intact water landing. The mission marks a significant milestone in the rocket's development.

title: ESA Puts €65M Behind Europe’s First Lunar Ice Rover
summary: ESA has committed €65 million to support Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. This marks a significant step in Europe's lunar exploration efforts.

title: Lunar Outpost Plans to Fly NVIDIA Chips to the Moon
summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA's chips to the Moon, merging the semiconductor and lunar exploration industries. This move highlights the growing intersection of advanced computing and space missions.

title: A Deep Dive into the Bluetooth Satellite Connectivity Market Following the FCC’s Proposal
summary: The FCC is proposing to open unlicensed Bluetooth and Wi-Fi frequencies for space-based communications. This move could expand satellite connectivity capabilities.

title: FCC Filings Show Eutelsat is Working on a New 528-sat Constellation Beyond OneWeb
summary: Eutelsat is developing a new constellation of 528 satellites, separate from its OneWeb program, as indicated by recent FCC filings. The company's Next program may not yet be fully developed.

title: NASA Puts $2B Price Tag on Nuclear Mars Mission
summary: NASA has estimated a $2 billion cost for the Space Reactor-1 Freedom, a fission-powered spacecraft intended for Mars missions. This marks a significant investment in nuclear propulsion technology for interplanetary travel.

title: Intel Authorization Act Proposes Limiting Commercial EO Access
summary: The Intel Authorization Act aims to restrict commercial Earth observation (EO) satellite operators from sharing data with the public, framing EO data as a privilege rather than a right. This move seeks to increase government control over EO data dissemination.

title: The UK Scraps the Department in Charge of UKSA
summary: The UK has decided to abolish the department overseeing the UK Space Agency (UKSA) during the Farnborough Air Show. This move comes as the country highlights its aerospace achievements under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

title: The UK and Space Florida Launch Joint Fund
summary: The UK and Space Florida have launched a joint fund to support projects with partners from both regions. This initiative aims to foster collaboration between the UK and Florida's space sectors.

title: Via Satellite Rising Stars of 2026
summary: Via Satellite announces its third class of 25 Rising Stars for 2026, highlighting young professionals shaping the future of the space and satellite industry.

title: Building the Connectivity Backbone for the Next Era of Lunar Exploration
summary: The article discusses the development of a connectivity backbone to support future lunar exploration efforts. It highlights the evolution of space-based services and their expansion to support lunar missions.

title: How Fast Can You Build a Satellite? Inside the Smallsat Manufacturing Market
summary: The article discusses the challenges of small satellite manufacturing, highlighting the balance between speed, cost, and flexibility in project management. It explores the dynamics of the smallsat market and the unique constraints faced in space industry projects.

title: Thermodynamics Does Not Care About Your Form Factor
summary: A spacecraft program faces challenges in thermal management as engineers realize the difficulty of dissipating heat once the structure is already built. The article emphasizes the importance of considering thermal design early in spacecraft development.

title: In the AI Era, Constellations Emerge As a New Strategic Class of Assets
summary: The article discusses how constellations of satellites are becoming a new strategic class of assets in the AI era, expanding beyond traditional military space dominance by a few nations. It highlights the shift from large, expensive satellites to more distributed and capable systems.

title: 10 Smallsat Startups to Watch in 2026
summary: Via Satellite releases a list of 10 smallsat startups to watch in 2026, highlighting early-stage companies globally that are in Series A funding or earlier stages.

title: New Horizons  for the Smallsat Industry
summary: Via Satellite rebrands to focus on the smallsat industry, introducing the third group of Rising Stars. This marks a new direction for the publication to highlight advancements in small satellite technology.

title: NASA to Support New Glenn Hot Fire Testing at Stennis Space Center
summary: NASA and Blue Origin will collaborate on second stage hot fire testing for the New Glenn rocket at NASA’s Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. This partnership aims to advance the development of the New Glenn rocket.

title: Two Galileo Satellites Enter Service for Europe
summary: Two new Galileo satellites, SAT 33 and SAT 34, have entered service, enhancing Europe's satellite navigation system. The European Space Agency (ESA) announced their operational status, boosting the system's capability and resilience.

title: Telco CEOs Shut Down the Idea of Satellite MVNO, Say LEO Isn’t a Threat to Broadband
summary: Telco CEOs dismissed the idea of forming an MVNO agreement with satellite providers, asserting that LEO satellite broadband is not a significant threat to their broadband services.
